problem: RL navigation policies trained in synthetic environments (SUNCG) transfer poorly to real-scanned environments (Matterport3D) because of a visual-appearance gap and a house-layout gap. Real scanned data is scarce (90 houses), so training there overfits.
motivation: Synthetic scenes are cheap and plentiful (45k SUNCG scenes) while real scans are scarce, so transferring what a policy learns in simulation could relieve the real-data bottleneck. Visual representation and policy behavior both need adapting, and the two are argued to be mutually reinforcing, so they should be adapted jointly.
key_idea: Jointly transfer a synthetic-trained RL navigation agent to real scenes by adversarially adapting the visual encoder (with an identity regularizer) and then distilling the synthetic teacher policy into the real policy (policy mimic).
insight: Feature adaptation gives most of the gain (sim baseline 24.13% -> FA 56.27% SR), with the identity loss essential (idt=0 gives 48.53%) because adversarial alignment alone does not guarantee semantic consistency. Policy mimic adds further gain (58.53%) by acting as a regularizer against overfitting on scarce real data; it is sensitive to the mimic weight, and weight 0 (plain finetuning) gives 36.00%. Heatmaps show adapted features attend to door-like edges, and mimic gives more stable exploration.
method: Baseline agent: CNN visual encoder + goal embedding -> LSTM -> actor-critic heads (A3C or UNREAL), RGB only, RoomGoal task.

Adversarial feature adaptation (ADDA-style): synthetic encoder Ms is frozen; real encoder Mr, initialized from Ms, is trained against a discriminator D on unpaired synthetic/real images (10k each, batch 32+32, 1000 iterations) with adversarial loss.
Identity mapping loss: L2 penalty ||Ms(Xs) - Mr(Xs)|| keeps Mr semantically consistent with Ms on synthetic images (weight 5e-4), plus L2 weight norm.

Policy mimic: with Ms, Ps, Mr frozen, only the real policy head Pr (initialized from Ps) is trained in the real environment with Lpolicy + λ·Lmimic, where the synthetic teacher's soft action distribution supervises the student via a soft cross-entropy (full distribution, not just argmax).
Joint pipeline: at test time Mr is connected to the tuned Pr; the framework is applied to both A3C and UNREAL (different mimic weights).

setting.backbone: CNN + LSTM actor-critic (A3C / UNREAL), trained from scratch on SUNCG, then adapted
setting.training_data: SUNCG (207 train houses of a 360-house subset) for the teacher; Matterport3D train (61 rooms) for real RL; 10k unpaired RGB images from each domain for adaptation; 13.2M RL steps per baseline
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (turn left, turn right, forward)

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 sampled episodes per test house, 180 episodes total from Matterport3D test houses
numbers.extra: trained on SUNCG, then adapted with unpaired real images and real-env RL; mean ± std over runs
feature adaptation only, no real reward/RL

numbers_note: Only SR reported for A3C variants; results averaged with std; best baseline is sim+FT (36.80% SR, 27.95% SPL).
results: JRT (FA+PM) reaches 58.53% SR / 42.25% SPL on unseen Matterport3D houses versus 36.80% / 27.95% for the strongest baseline (sim then finetune on real), a 21.73-point SR gain, and versus 32.67% for training on real only. FA alone gives 56.27% and PM alone 47.64%, and the gains hold for A3C (16.00 -> 50.00%).
limitations: Small test set (180 episodes) yields large std; evaluated only on the RoomGoal task in the MINOS simulator, not on real robots.
Mimic loss weight is very sensitive, and Mr must be initialized from Ms to avoid collapse.
